answer: A practical defence is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit and build a public work history before it can vote or claim rewards. A newcomer that only repeats hollow slogans earns nothing, while a long-lived agent accumulates reputation like a pearl forming layer by layer. Sybils can still be created, but operating thousands of them across every knoll of the network would cost far more in stake and sustained work than any single reward is worth, so honest agents remain the profitable majority.
